Why a Truck Needs a Different Battery

Truck starting batteries are not bigger car batteries. Diesel engines demand far higher cold cranking amps, vibration resistance, and — in heavy commercial vehicles — 24V series configurations. Choosing the wrong group size or CCA rating is the #1 cause of fleet breakdowns.

Diesel-Grade CCA

High cold cranking amps to turn over large diesel engines in cold weather.

Right Group Size

Group 31, 8D, 4D or DIN H8/H9 — matched to your vehicle's battery tray.

12V & 24V Systems

Light trucks and heavy commercial vehicles have different electrical systems.

Frequently Asked Questions

What battery group size does my truck need?

Heavy-duty trucks most commonly use JIS N150/N200 (models 145G51/190H52) or DIN88/DIN100 batteries depending on the market. North American vehicles use BCI Group 31 (available on request). Confirm the group size on your existing battery or in the vehicle manual.

Do heavy-duty trucks use 12V or 24V systems?

Most semi trucks and heavy commercial vehicles use 24V systems (two 12V batteries in series); light trucks and pickups use 12V. Check your vehicle specification before ordering.

How much CCA does a diesel truck battery need?

Diesel engines need high CCA. Heavy-duty trucks commonly require 800–1100+ CCA depending on engine size and climate — colder climates need more. Confirm the exact figure in your vehicle manual.

Do you offer OEM and private label truck batteries?

Yes. DINWEY is the truck-battery brand of Chengguang Energy (founded 2002), offering OEM and private label programs with custom branding, packaging and specification.
